item.title: What It's Like to Be...a Baker - By Dan Heath - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: Tinkering with the recipe for gingerbread cake until it's right, adjusting to the variability of local grains, and cherishing the quiet mornings when the sun fills the bakery windows with Sophie Williams, a baker in Bellingham, Washington.

item.title: What It's Like to Be...a London Divorce Lawyer - By Dan Heath - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: Negotiating cases in which neither spouse wants custody of the cat, setting clients' expectations about what's legally possible (versus what feels "right"), and finding hope in people's ability to bounce back from dark times with Lucy Stewart-Gould, a divorce lawyer in London.

item.title: How to Embed Equity in Your Research, Despite the Backlash - by Crystal Hall - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: The current political moment makes equity-grounded research harder. But that's precisely the reason we need to keep doing it.

item.title: Why Rational Choice Theory Should Not Be the Standard for Good Decisions - by Barry Schwartz - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: A half century of research on how people make decisions has shown that rational choice theory fails to describe how people do choose. Nevertheless, it has remained at the center of things, as the normative answer to questions about how people should choose.

item.title: RECORDING & RESOURCES—Neuropaz 2026: Hard Truths & Paths Forward - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: View all the sessions from Neuropaz 2026—an online event exploring the latest work and thinking at the intersection of behavioral science and peace and conflict. Plus, access additional resources from all of our speakers.

item.title: What It's Like to Be...a Health Inspector - By Dan Heath - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: Suspending the licenses of unsafe restaurant operators, hunting down the origins of foodborne illness outbreaks, and eliciting truthful answers from anxious managers with Justin Dwyer, a health inspector in Peoria, Illinois.

item.title: What It Takes to Make Good Decisions: Judgment, Not Calculation - by Barry Schwartz - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: The real work in deciding is not in the calculation, but all the thinking that surrounds it.

item.title: What It's Like to Be...a Lineman - By Dan Heath - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: Wiring a neighborhood back to life after a tornado, coveting the work of helicopter linemen in Faraday suits, and surviving the collapse of a rotten utility pole with Elden Rivas, a journeyman lineman in Houston, Texas.

item.title: Facts and the Fight for Moral High Ground - by Gwen Ottinger - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: How science can get it right and still miss the point.

item.title: 'Looking Backward' to the Future - Behavioral Scientist
item.description: When American author Edward Bellamy published his utopian novel Looking Backward: 2000 – 1887 in 1888, he didn’t know that it would be one of the best-selling books of the era; that it would inspire a political groups around the world; or that some of the most prominent intellectuals of the time would count it as an influence on their thinking.
